Definition: from the alternate of G5143; a race, i.e. (figuratively) career:--course.
BiblicalUsage: A course, a race, the course Paul was determined to finish with joy, testifying to the gospel of the grace of God. At the end he could say he had fought the good fight and finished his course, and John said the same about his own course when he told the crowds he was not the Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe life is a course to finish, not a sprint to win, and the joy is in finishing it faithfully. Paul counted his life dear only so far as he could finish, and I want to be able to say the same at the end.
